column1: # spec: guard-kit/SPEC.md §Testing — rule `background_no_record`'s PowerShell harness arm: the
# background-cases.tsv grammar, each row fed as a PowerShell payload to the same member.
# rule `background_no_record` — an unrecorded launch blocks; the canonical LF-terminated record
# write discharges it, a CRLF or UTF-16 write does not, and neither does one outside the scratch dir

column3: Set-Content -NoNewline -Path .tmp/build.run -Value "pid=$PID run=build`n"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp/build.run }
set-content -n .tmp\build.run "pid=$PID run=build`n"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp\build.run }
Set-Content -Path .tmp/build.run -Value "pid=$PID run=build`n"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp/build.run }
Set-Content -NoNewline -Path .tmp/build.run -Value "pid=$PID run=build"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp/build.run }
Set-Content -NoNewline -Encoding Unicode -Path .tmp/build.run -Value "pid=$PID run=build`n"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp/build.run }
pid=$PID run=build > .tmp/build.run; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item .tmp/build.run }
Set-Content -NoNewline -Path tracked.run -Value "pid=$PID run=build`n"; try { pwsh -File tools/build.ps1 } finally { Remove-Item tracked.run }
